subject: Attribution for latency/uptime in private deployment - HelioHealth request
messages:
From: David Liu <david.liu@heliohealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@heliohealth.com
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: attribution for latency/uptime in our private deployment

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for the onboarding call this morning. We're excited to get Redwood Private running in our Boston colo. One quick governance item came up with our infra team: because HelioHealth will be controlling the border routers, BGP peerings, and our on-prem firewall stack, we need to formally capture an "attribution" approach for any uptime/latency obligations in the contract.

Specifically, we want to ensure Redwood's SLA doesn't count network-layer incidents that are caused entirely by our edge peering, carrier issues, or on-prem routing misconfiguration. Can your team propose (a) a short carveout clause and (b) a minimal evidence protocol so we can rapidly validate cause during incidents?

Attached: network-diagram.png (high-level), helio_initial_request.pdf (one-pager from our infra team).

We'd like to move quickly because procurement wants the addendum before the production go-live next month.

Best,
David Liu
Head of Infrastructure
HelioHealth

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, David Liu <david.liu@heliohealth.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2027 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fw: Request: attribution for latency/uptime in our private deployment

Vanessa / team — technical POV below. TL;DR: we can accept a customer-network carveout but need three operational controls to make it workable.

1) Measurement points: all SLA metrics must be measured at our API ingress and at the model-serving egress inside the customer pod. We will report token-level latency and request success rate from our side; any network hop outside the customer-managed VPC edge must be excluded if Helio proves fault originated in their edge.

2) Minimum telemetry: to adjudicate, we require at least one of the following for the incident window: 
   - OTLP traces with endpoint-level spans for request ingress/egress
   - Flow logs (5-tuple) for the border routers covering the incident interval
   - Prefix reachability checks (BGP updates) and simple ping/latency probes to our collector
We typically ask for 72 hours retention for incident evidence; anything longer is negotiable per account.

3) Joint incident runbook and quick triage: a shared incident channel and pre-approved playbook that includes an agreed set of steps and Who/When to escalate. If Helio cannot produce the required telemetry within the incident window, the incident is treated as "undetermined" and the SLA will default to our measurement.

Suggested carveout language (draft):
"Redwood does not count as downtime or SLA breach any unavailability or latency degradation demonstrably caused by the customer's network, including but not limited to customer-managed border-router misconfiguration, carrier/peering issues outside Redwood's control, or on-prem firewall policies. The customer must provide telemetry consistent with the Evidence Protocol (Appendix A) to demonstrate attribution within the incident review window. Failure to provide required evidence will result in the incident being adjudicated on Redwood's measured metrics."

I'm happy to tighten the legal wording with Naomi. From an engineering perspective, we should also offer a fallback: in production-critical tenants we can enable a "hosted-egress" path for a limited set of requests to guarantee availability at higher cost.

-Marcus
Sr. Engineering Manager, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>

Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fw: Request: attribution for latency/uptime in our private deployment

Vanessa / all — legal and compliance notes. We can accept the carveout language Marcus proposed with a few clarifications:

- Evidence scope: specify exact artifacts acceptable (OTLP traces with trace IDs and timestamps, flow logs showing 5-tuple and timestamps, BGP update logs). We should avoid open-ended "packet captures" as they risk PII exposure; if pcap is necessary, it must be redacted and transferred under an NDA appendix.
- Retention and access: require 90 days of incident evidence retention for the duration of the contract, with an audit window and read-only access for Redwood during an active incident review.
- KMS: if Helio wants to provide encrypted archives, they must document KMS control-plane access and key rotation policies.

I'll attach an "Evidence Protocol Checklist" (evidence_protocol_checklist.xlsx) and a short SLA addendum template. If Helio insists on shorter retention, we can allow it for non-production tiers only.

Naomi Feldman
Head of Security & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
Attachment: evidence_protocol_checklist.xlsx

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: David Liu <david.liu@heliohealth.com>, HelioHealth Legal <legal@heliohealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Sep 2027 10:00:00 -0700
Subject: Redwood proposed SLA addendum and next steps (HelioHealth)

David — thanks for the clear ask and for sharing the diagram. After internal review we can accept a customer-network attribution carveout with the controls below. I've attached a draft SLA addendum (rwi_sla_addendum_helio_draft_v1.pdf) that captures the language and the Evidence Protocol (Appendix A).

Summary of the agreed controls:
- Carveout for "customer-managed network events" with explicit examples.
- Required evidence: OTLP traces or flow logs (5-tuple) + prefix reachability history for the incident window.
- Evidence retention: 90 days minimum during the contract; pcap only under NDA and redaction policy.
- Joint incident runbook and pre-established channel for incident response.
- Option: enable a hosted-egress fallback for production-critical routes (additional fees apply).

Next steps:
1) Please review the attached addendum and the Evidence Protocol appendix.
2) If acceptable, HelioHealth legal to return redlines by EOD next Thursday.
3) Engineering onboarding: schedule a 2-hour telemetry handoff with our runtime team within two weeks of signed addendum.

If you want, we can stand up a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the appendix. Happy to coordinate.

Best regards,
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Solutions
Redwood Inference

--
